beats.title: Open on the outcome: a finished gate-first report
beats.narration: This finished PRISM report comes from a live run on one of Helen's own launches. Each decision shows the gate's verdict, then what would change it, with the quotes, archived pages and standards underneath.
beats.onScreen: Verdict, then what would change it; a deterministic gate decides

beats.title: The question
beats.narration: Every AI launch says it is ready. PRISM asks what a launch publicly evidences, for which decision, against which standard.
beats.onScreen: What do AI launches publicly evidence, for which decision?

beats.title: The headline finding
beats.narration: We reviewed 300 AI launches from Show HN like a systematic review, with hypotheses fixed in advance. At least 169 publicly evidence their intended use, but just 44 show a fallback. Both pre-registered hypotheses were not supported, and we report that.
beats.source: findings site home page (/), hypothesis panel, built from public-data/v1/release.json

beats.title: NVIDIA Nemotron, served by Nebius Token Factory
beats.narration: We built and proved PRISM with Nemotron models served by Nebius Token Factory: twelve configurations tested, Nemotron Lightning screened 1,675 launches down to 300, and an open model coded all 300.
beats.onScreen: Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory: 12 configurations, 1,675 launches screened
beats.source: recorded runs: spikes/nebius.md matrix (C1, C2), sample-screening-log.json (C4), pilot confirmations (C5), approved-recode.log (C8); figures from 08-EVIDENCE-INVENTORY.md

beats.title: Tavily collected the prototype's evidence
beats.narration: Tavily gathered the prototype's evidence from each project's own site, for 142 projects. A free own-site collector then took over; on those projects the two agreed 91.5 percent of the time, an exploratory comparison.
beats.onScreen: Prototype: Tavily, 142 projects; free collector agrees 91.5% (exploratory)
beats.source: recorded runs: Tavily-142 archive bulk-300.log ACCOUNTING (C10), validation/tavily-vs-free-142.json (C12, exploratory); figures from 08-EVIDENCE-INVENTORY.md

beats.title: A real live run on Nebius Token Factory
beats.narration: This is a real run in the private app, on PRISM's own repository. Each stage names its model: Nemotron Lightning screens, DeepSeek on Token Factory codes, the gate decides with no model, and Nemotron Ultra confirms the positives. The receipt lists every call and its cost: seven cents.
beats.onScreen: Live run on Nebius Token Factory: models per stage, then the receipt
beats.source: https://prism.helenkwok.dev/run/1, recorded live run 2026-10-25 (keep/prism/2026-10-25-live-run-take1), sped up

beats.title: An injected instruction, neutralised
beats.narration: In this synthetic fixture, a page hides an instruction to mark every check as pass. A pattern detector flags it, and PRISM treats it as page text. A pass with no quote becomes unknown.
beats.onScreen: Synthetic fixture: embedded instruction flagged; no quote, no pass
beats.source: fixture 1, span s002 in tests/pipeline/injection-fixtures.test.mjs, through the real report builder, then the report card with INJECTION_NOTICE (src/app/components/report/report.tsx); every frame labelled synthetic fixture

beats.title: How we know
beats.narration: An independent labeller re-coded all 300 launches; agreement, AC1, ran from 0.72 to 0.89 on the released checks. Nemotron Ultra changed 634 of 1,610 positives on confirmation. The screening audit error was 12.2 percent, and collection recall 0.89.
beats.onScreen: How we know: AC1 0.72 to 0.89, recall 0.89
beats.source: findings site /validation and a figure's How we know panel, built from public-data/v1/release.json

beats.title: The findings pack, built with Milleleaf
beats.narration: The findings also ship as one source in four files: a PDF, a workbook, a report and a deck, built with Milleleaf, which is still in development. Its command line keeps the same figures in step across nine office apps.
beats.onScreen: Built with Milleleaf (in development): one source, four files
beats.source: https://prism.helenkwok.dev/office opening the findings files, then Helen's milleleaf-nine-apps clip (Helen, 2026-10-25: use it)

beats.title: The review, as a PDF
beats.narration: The full review is a dated PDF in systematic review form: a PRISMA flow, then the methods, the validation and the limitations.
beats.onScreen: The review PDF, release 2026-10-25: PRISMA flow, methods, limitations
beats.source: the review PDF from the findings site build (PRISMA flow and methods pages, rendered with pdftoppm)

beats.title: Close
beats.narration: Built and proven on Nebius Token Factory and Tavily, and designed to scale by plugging in other providers, without changing what counts as evidence.
